scenes.title: Clear but Not Mean
scenes.summary: Standard words give clarity but meanness, as in Cleophon and Sthenelus; unfamiliar words give dignity, but all metaphor makes a riddle and all rare words a barbarism. Diction must be a blend.

scenes.title: Lengthenings and Their Mockers
scenes.summary: Lengthenings and alterations serve both clarity and distinction; Euclides the elder's parodies miss the point, though moderation is needed.

scenes.title: One Word Makes the Difference
scenes.summary: Substitute standard words and a verse falls flat: Aeschylus' Philoctetes and Euripides', and Homer's lines rewritten.

scenes.title: Ariphrades' Mockery
scenes.summary: Ariphrades mocked the tragedians for phrases no one would say, not seeing that this is what lifts them.

scenes.title: The Gift for Metaphor
scenes.summary: The greatest thing is a gift for metaphor, which cannot be learned, for it is seeing likeness; compounds suit dithyramb, rare words heroic verse, metaphors iambics.
